title: Benchmark scenario
description: A scenario is one pinned, runnable recipe for a workload at a specific software stack. A workload is the thing measured and groups scenarios; a scenario validates. Two scenarios sharing a slug but pinning different stacks are the comparable pair.

slug.description: Stable machine name for this scenario. Used in paths and cross-references, so it must describe the workload rather than the cluster it happened to run on.

workload.description: The workload class this scenario measures. Groups scenarios; matches the parent directory under benchmarks/workloads/.

intent.description: Why this scenario exists and what it characterizes.

topology.description: The cluster shape this scenario was validated on. Describes one bed; see `sizing` for how the workload scales to a different one.

node_type.description: Publicly marketed hardware description — part names and observable properties such as core count, memory and NIC line rate. Enough for a reader to judge whether a number transfers to their own hardware.

sizing.description: How the workload scales. `derivation` is the rule that lets a reader size this to THEIR cluster — the epic's Definition of Done requires it. `observed` is what the rule resolved to for the published run, which is what makes the result reproducible and comparable.

rule.description: Human-readable statement of how run parameters follow from cluster shape.

observed.description: Concrete parameter values for the published run. Keys are workload-specific.

stack.description: The software stack this scenario was validated against. Required in full: two scenarios of the same workload at different stack versions must be distinguishable and comparable, which is only true if every component is pinned.

build.description: Provenance of the running build. `vendor` denotes a distribution-specific build without naming its registry path, which is a sanitization rule class. Keeping this field is what lets two runs on different builds still be compared honestly.

dataplane.description: Optional dataplane component and version, e.g. OVS for OVN-Kubernetes.

engine.description: The benchmark engine actually executed, named as the upstream project. A scenario that pinned a wrapper instead could not be reconstructed by anyone who does not have that wrapper.

version.description: Release tag where the engine publishes one, otherwise a commit SHA on a best-effort basis. Not every upstream engine is versioned, and for runs already completed the exact commit is not always recoverable -- record what is known.

etcd.description: etcd version. Optional only because the measurement tooling does not yet collect it; required in spirit and should be filled whenever known.

simulator.description: Node simulator, where the scenario ran against fake nodes rather than real machines. Optional because most scenarios use neither. REQUIRED whenever one was used: a node count produced by a simulator is not the same measurement as the same count of real machines, and a reader who cannot tell which they are looking at will read a simulated tier as hardware. `topology` stays the real cluster the simulator ran on; the simulated node counts belong in sizing.observed.

version.description: Release tag, otherwise a commit SHA. Where a scenario does not depend on a specific release, say which interface it does depend on instead -- that is more useful to a reader than a version they have no reason to match.

simulates.description: What the simulator stands in for, so a reader knows exactly which part of the result is not real hardware.

engine_config.description: Relative path to the checked-in, engine-native config this scenario runs. Mandatory by design: a scenario with nothing to point at is not a recipe and must not validate. The path is additionally checked to resolve.

metrics.description: The metrics contract. Split into the small set every scenario carries and whatever this workload actually measures — result shapes differ sharply across workloads and the contract is designed for that, not around it.

slo.description: The pass/fail rules this scenario is judged against, inline rather than by reference — a reader must be able to judge their own run from the scenario alone.

applies_to.description: Optional scope, e.g. the network paths or sizes a threshold applies to.

dashboard.description: Relative path, or list of paths, to the Grafana dashboard(s) this scenario is read with. Dashboards describe subsystems rather than workloads, so they live in benchmarks/dashboards/<kubernetes-minor>/ and are referenced rather than bundled. A directory is valid from its release until the next one exists, so reference the newest at or below this scenario's stack.kubernetes.

alerts.description: Relative path, or list of paths, to the alerting rules a run is watched with. Shared rules live in benchmarks/alerts/<kubernetes-minor>/ and follow the same newest-at-or-below rule as dashboards; rules scoped to one workload sit beside the scenario. Optional -- but a scenario shipping none should say so in its README. Thresholds calibrated for one environment may be wrong in another.

prerequisites.description: What a cluster must satisfy before this scenario is meaningful.

baseline_validation.description: Ordered checks to run before trusting a result from this scenario.

upstream.description: How to run this scenario using only the upstream project. Structured rather than prose so presence and shape stay machine-checkable — this asserts the scenario names its engine, version, config and argv, NOT that argv executes unmodified on another cluster.

engine_version.description: Release tag where the engine publishes one, otherwise a commit SHA on a best-effort basis. Should match stack.engine.version.

config.description: Relative path to the config passed to the engine. Checked to resolve.
